sections.h2: What does a Florida warranty deed do?
sections.html:
A Florida warranty deed moves title to land and carries the grantor's promise that the title is good. The statutory form says the grantor "does hereby fully warrant the title to said land, and will defend the same against the lawful claims of all persons whomsoever."

That promise is the difference between a warranty deed and a quit claim deed, which hands over whatever interest the grantor holds without vouching for it. Buyers who pay full price, and their lenders, usually expect the stronger form. Section 689.02 sets out the sample wording, and a deed may be built on it.

sections.h2: What must a warranty deed contain to be valid and recordable?
sections.html:
The deed must be in writing, signed in front of two subscribing witnesses. Section 689.01 requires no seal, and it allows the witnessing to happen by audio-video technology.

Recording adds a second layer of rules. Under s. 695.26, a clerk may not record the instrument unless the points below appear on it:

  • Each signer's name printed beneath the signature, with a post-office address.
  • The name and address of the natural person who prepared the deed.
  • Each witness's name printed beneath the signature, with an address.
  • The name of the notary or other officer taking the acknowledgment, printed under that signature.
  • A 3-inch by 3-inch blank space at the top right of the first page and a 1-inch by 3-inch space at the top right of every later page, left for the clerk.
  • The name and address of each grantee.

Out-of-state signings, court orders and wills are carved out of that section. If a clerk accepts a deed that misses a step, the statute says the recording and its constructive notice still stand.

sections.h2: Does a Florida deed need a parcel number?
sections.html:
The statutory form includes a blank for the property appraiser's parcel identification number, but a missing or wrong number does not void the deed.

Section 689.02(2) says the number, when available, should be entered before recording. It is not part of the legal description and cannot replace it. Copy the legal description exactly from the prior deed or a survey, then add the parcel number as a convenience for the clerk and the appraiser.

sections.h2: How much is the documentary stamp tax on a Florida deed?
sections.html:
Under s. 201.02, the deed tax is 70 cents on each $100 of consideration. The Department of Revenue lists Miami-Dade County separately, at 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax that does not apply to a document transferring only a single-family dwelling.

Consideration is read broadly. It covers money paid, the discharge of an obligation, and any mortgage or encumbrance on the property, whether or not the buyer assumes it. So a deed that moves a mortgaged house for "ten dollars" can still produce tax on the loan balance.

The department states that all parties to the document are liable no matter who agrees to pay, and that if one party is exempt, a non-exempt party pays. The clerk collects the tax when the deed is recorded. A deed is taxable whether or not it is recorded.

sections.h2: Which transfers escape the deed tax, and which do not?
sections.html:
The exemptions are narrow, and the Department of Revenue says there is no specific exemption for estate planning transfers.

Deed types and documentary stamp tax, as listed by the Department of Revenue
DocumentTaxable?
Warranty, special warranty, quit claim, trustee's and life estate deedsListed as taxable
Deed in lieu of foreclosure, contract for deed, certificate of titleListed as taxable
Personal representative's deed under a probated willListed as not taxable
Spousal homestead deed where the only consideration is a mortgage; divorce deed for the marital homeExempt under s. 201.02(7)

A lady bird deed has its own treatment. A 2020 Department of Revenue advisement concluded that one on the facts presented, where the life tenants kept full powers, transferred no present beneficial interest and was not subject to documentary stamp tax. Ask a Florida attorney whether your deed fits those facts.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed cost at the clerk's office?
sections.html:
Recording charges are set by s. 28.24(13), and they are separate from the stamp tax.

  • $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, for instruments up to 14 by 8.5 inches.
  • $1.00 for each name beyond four.
  • A Public Records Modernization Trust Fund charge of $1.00 on the first page and $0.50 on each additional page.
  • An additional $4 per page technology charge.

Your county clerk can confirm the current total for your page count before you submit.

sections.h2: What other stamp taxes can appear around a sale?
sections.html:
Mortgage paperwork is taxed separately from the deed. The Department of Revenue prints 35 cents per $100 of the amount secured for mortgages and notes, with the tax on a note capped at $2,450 and no cap on mortgages.

A foreclosure produces a certificate of title, and s. 201.02(9) computes its tax on the highest and best bid at the sale. For an ordinary sale between private parties, expect the deed tax to be the main figure, and ask your closing agent whether the buyer's new loan adds its own charges.

sections.h2: How should a seller prepare a deed before closing?
sections.html:
Assemble the pieces early, because a clerk can reject an instrument at the counter and the closing then slips.

  • Pull the legal description from your vesting deed and copy it character for character.
  • Confirm the exact way each grantor's name appears in the record, and use the same spelling.
  • Line up two adult witnesses and a notary on the signing day, or ask the title company about remote witnessing.
  • Print every name and mailing address where the statute wants it.
  • Leave the top right corner of each page clear for the clerk.

Then confirm with the closing agent what stamp tax will be due and who funds it.

sections.h2: How does a deed affect property taxes after the sale?
sections.html:
A sale, foreclosure or other transfer of title is a change of ownership, and the property goes back to just value on the following January 1. The seller's Save Our Homes cap does not follow the house.

Exceptions include transfers between spouses and certain transfers at death. A quitclaim to a relative is not an exception just because no money changes hands. Buyers should file for their own homestead exemption with the county property appraiser by March 1, and should look into portability if they held a homestead elsewhere in the state.

faqs.q: Do both spouses have to sign a Florida warranty deed?
faqs.a: Not always, but a married owner should confirm whether the home is homestead before signing. Homestead rules on spousal joinder sit outside the statutes reviewed here, so ask a Florida title attorney or title company. Any signer must still follow the two-witness and printed-name rules.

faqs.q: Can I use a warranty deed to give a house to my child?
faqs.a: Yes, but the transfer is a change of ownership for assessment purposes and can carry stamp tax on any mortgage balance. The Department of Revenue lists no estate planning exemption. Talk with an attorney before choosing a deed type.

faqs.q: Who pays the documentary stamp tax on a deed?
faqs.a: The parties decide among themselves, but the state holds all of them liable. If one party is exempt, a non-exempt party must pay. The clerk collects it at recording.

faqs.q: Is a deed valid if the clerk's recording was imperfect?
faqs.a: Generally yes. Section 695.26(4) says a clerk's failure to follow the recording checklist does not impair the recording or its constructive notice. Fix defects anyway, because title companies will flag them.

faqs.q: Where is the deed tax paid?
faqs.a: Pay it to the county clerk when the deed is recorded. If a taxable document is never recorded, the tax goes to the Department of Revenue instead.

faqs.q: Is a warranty deed the same as a deed in lieu of foreclosure?
faqs.a: No. A deed in lieu is a separate instrument a borrower gives a lender, and the Department of Revenue lists it as taxable. A warranty deed is the usual form for an ordinary sale.
